title: too much / too many / not enough / enough
grammarTitle: too much / too many / not enough / enough
grammarNote: "Too much/many" выражают ИЗБЫТОК — больше, чем нужно или хорошо. "Enough" выражает ДОСТАТОЧНОСТЬ. "Not enough" = недостаточно. Эти слова часто выражают ПРОБЛЕМУ. Порядок слов: too much/many + noun; not + adjective/adverb + enough; enough + noun; adjective + enough.

grammarTable.subject: too much
grammarTable.example: "There's too much oil." / "I ate too much yesterday." (UC / no noun)

grammarTable.subject: too many
grammarTable.example: "There are too many ingredients." / "I bought too many eggs." (C, plural)

grammarTable.subject: enough
grammarTable.example: "We have enough flour." / "Is there enough time?"

grammarTable.subject: not enough
grammarTable.example: "There's not enough salt." / "We don't have enough eggs." (UC or C)

grammarTable.subject: adj + enough
grammarTable.example: "The dough isn't thick enough." / "She's good enough to apply."

grammarTable.subject: not adj + enough
grammarTable.example: "The soup isn't hot enough." / "I wasn't fast enough."

grammarExtra.title: too much vs too many — same rule as much/many

rows.example: "There's too much salt." / "Don't eat too much sugar." / "We have too much rice."
"There are too many onions." / "I bought too many eggs." / "She has too many classes."
"I ate too much." (no noun — uncountable feeling implied)
"There isn't enough flour." / "We don't have enough time." (UC)
"There aren't enough eggs." / "There aren't enough chairs." (C)
"There ISN'T enough water." / "There AREN'T enough eggs." (match the noun)
"The room is warm ENOUGH." / "She's old ENOUGH to decide." (after adjective!)
"The soup isn't hot ENOUGH." / "He's not tall ENOUGH." (problem = quality)
"There's ENOUGH food." / "We have ENOUGH time." (before noun)
✗ "The room is enough warm." → ✅ "The room is warm enough."

grammarExtra.title: too vs very — an important difference

rows.example: "This is very spicy." = it's very spicy (I might like it or not)
"This is too spicy." = it's more spicy than I can eat — a PROBLEM!
"The dough is too sticky." → I can't work with it. Problem implied.
Problem → "too". No problem → "very". "Very good" ≠ "Too good (to eat here)."

grammarTip:
"Too" = проблема! "Enough" = достаточно:
① too much + UNCOUNTABLE (Oil is too much) → "There's too much oil."
② too many + COUNTABLE (Eggs are too many) → "There are too many eggs."
③ not enough + any noun → "There isn't enough salt." / "There aren't enough eggs."
④ adjective + ENOUGH (after!) → "The soup is hot enough." / "It's not sweet enough."

💡 "Too" всегда указывает на ПРОБЛЕМУ:
"The soup is very hot." (нейтрально — возможно, мне нравится)
"The soup is too hot." (проблема — я не могу есть!)

⚠️ Порядок:
"enough" + noun: enough food ✅
adjective + "enough": warm enough ✅
✗ никогда "enough warm"!

exercises.text: Don't add ___ salt — it will ruin the dish.
exercises.hint: "salt" = uncountable → "too much salt". "Don't add TOO MUCH salt." ✅

exercises.text: I bought ___ eggs — I don't know what to do with them all.
exercises.hint: "eggs" = countable → "too many eggs". "I bought TOO MANY eggs." ✅

exercises.text: The manti were flat — there was ___ filling.
exercises.hint: "not enough filling" = insufficient quantity. "There was NOT ENOUGH filling." ✅

exercises.text: The soup needs more salt. Which sentence describes this?
opts: The soup has too much salt.
The soup has too many salt.
exercises.hint: "not salty enough" = needs more salt. "The soup isn't salty ENOUGH." ✅ (adjective + enough)

exercises.text: "The room is enough warm" is correct.
exercises.hint: ✅ "The room is warm ENOUGH." — adjective + enough. NEVER "enough + adjective"!

exercises.instruction: Complete with "too much", "too many", or "not enough".
exercises.text: The dough is too sticky because you added ___ water.
exercises.hint: "water" = uncountable → "too much water". "You added TOO MUCH water." ✅ (= excessive)

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form with adjective + enough.
exercises.text: The rice isn't ___ — we should cook it a bit more.
exercises.hint: adjective + enough (after the adjective!). "The rice isn't COOKED ENOUGH." ✅

exercises.text: "I have too much work this week." — The speaker feels:
opts: They have more work than they can manage
exercises.correct: They have more work than they can manage
exercises.hint: "too much" = excessive; more than what is good or manageable. A PROBLEM is implied.

exercises.text: There are ___ people and ___ chairs — some must stand.
exercises.hint: "too many people" (C, excessive) + "not enough chairs" (C, insufficient). ✅

exercises.text: "This coffee is ___ strong — I can't drink it."
exercises.hint: "too strong" = so strong it's a PROBLEM (can't drink it). "Very strong" = neutral (might enjoy it). ✅

exercises.text: The water is warm. Choose the correct sentence.
exercises.hint: adjective + ENOUGH (comes AFTER the adjective). "The water is warm ENOUGH." ✅

exercises.text: "She can't apply for the scholarship — she isn't ___ (experienced) ___."
exercises.hint: adjective + enough: "She isn't EXPERIENCED ENOUGH." = her experience level is insufficient. ✅

questions.text: "There's too much oil." — "too much" is used because:
questions.hint: "too much" = uncountable noun. "oil" is uncountable. "Too MUCH oil." ✅

questions.text: "There are too many onions." — "too many" because:
questions.hint: "too many" = countable plural noun. "onions" (one onion, two onions). "Too MANY onions." ✅
adjective + ENOUGH: "isn't hot ENOUGH" = needs to be hotter. ✅
"enough" before noun = sufficient. "We have ENOUGH chairs." ✅
"too" = problem/negative consequence. "Too much oil" = more oil than is good. A problem.
"flour" is uncountable. "There isn't enough flour." (not "There aren't enough flour." — wrong!)
"enough" with countable noun: "There aren't ENOUGH eggs." (= we need more eggs) ✅

questions.text: "The room is enough warm" is correct.
questions.hint: ✅ "The room is warm ENOUGH." — adjective + enough. NEVER "enough + adjective"!

questions.text: "This coffee is very strong." vs "This coffee is too strong." — difference?
questions.hint: "very strong" = neutral intensifier. "too strong" = excessively strong; a PROBLEM implied.

questions.text: "I ate too ___." (no noun — I ate an excessive amount)
questions.hint: "too much" alone (no noun) = excessive eating. "I ate TOO MUCH." = I ate more than I should have. ✅
"too hot" = excessive heat — a PROBLEM (e.g. can't eat it). "Very hot" = neutral, might still enjoy.

questions.text: "She's not old ___ to vote." (age is insufficient)
questions.hint: adjective + enough: "She's not old ENOUGH to vote." = her age is insufficient for voting. ✅

questions.text: "___ many students — not enough space." Choose correctly.
questions.hint: "students" = countable → "too MANY students". "Too many students — not enough space." ✅
adjective + enough (always after the adjective). "The room is BIG ENOUGH." ✅
"enough" works with BOTH: "isn't enough sugar" (UC) and "aren't enough oranges" (C). ✅

questions.text: "The manti had too ___ filling." (U.C. — filling is a mass)
